expected_differences: The actual account uses a D initial and demo-creator identity instead of Maya’s fixture portrait and name.
Production shows Available $34.00, Pending $0.00 and Lifetime $34.00; the Lab’s profile statistics and money amounts should not be copied.
The transaction uses its actual thumbnail, record title, Sep 9 date and Available state rather than the Lab’s recent-work fixtures.
The $25.00 payout minimum and manual payout explanation belong to production’s financial workflow.
The shell exposes notification counts of 2 and 3. The Lab’s $50.00 requested payout and fixture date are correctly not reproduced.
keep: Available first, with the dominant 44/48px money treatment, followed immediately by Request payout and its minimum.
Separate, unboxed Pending and Lifetime figures; no generic dashboard cards or floating financial surfaces.
Explicit fee reconciliation: $40.00 gross less $6.00 fee equals the displayed +$34.00.
Approved describes the work while Available independently describes the earning state.
Compact real source media, readable transaction copy, 16px page gutters and restrained separators.
Cobalt primary action and selected Earnings navigation, with the account switcher, search, messages and notifications retained.
review.readiness_note: Sign off the captured 390px resting state. Payout execution, navigation destinations, other backend states and motion cannot be verified from this capture and still require normal functional testing.
review.why: The mineral canvas, strong ink typography, cobalt payout decision and flat financial regions faithfully translate Frame Shift to Earnings rather than copying Profile’s layout. The money hierarchy is immediate: $34.00 Available, an enabled payout action with a $25.00 minimum, then Pending and Lifetime. The transaction exposes its source, literal earning state, date, gross amount, fee and net credit without clipping or obscuring the bottom navigation. The small thumbnail has a 12px gap to its facts; this settled ledger does not need an invented offset payment plane or Profile-style graphite masthead. No material visual drift or visible functional regression is evident.
review.verdict: Yes—Frame Shift is faithfully translated to Earnings, with clear real-money semantics and the visible production functionality intact.
